## (1) First message to the user

Before any question, here are the premises the design relies on. I checked them against the ticket's acceptance rows, the gather draft and `src/export/csv.ts`.

One premise is **contradicted**. The ticket's second row expects the export to include an owner column. `src/export/csv.ts:40` defines the table's columns as `const tableColumns = ["title", "status"];`, so the table has no owner column. The gather draft also says the CSV export reuses the table's column definitions. If we reuse those definitions unchanged, the export cannot include an owner. The design continues on this corrected fact unless you override it in your reply.

Two premises are **unverified**:

- **No export action on the reports page.** This comes from the gather draft. I had no reports-page source to confirm it. I'm assuming it is true, and I'll record it as an assumption.
- **The report data carries an owner value at all.** I found nothing in the files I have that shows an owner field on report rows. This is an implicit dependency of the owner-column row. I'll carry it into `## Problem` as unverified.

One premise is **supported**. There is an existing CSV serializer that takes its columns from the table, per `src/export/csv.ts:40` and the draft's pattern note. Ticket `acme/widgets#77` belongs to this repo per the overrides `repo: acme/widgets`. The ticket has no repo groups, so all three rows are attributed here.

The framing holds. I checked:

- the column contract at `src/export/csv.ts:40`;
- the draft's note that the serializer reuses the table's columns;
- the ticket's three rows against that contract.

Wiring a button to the existing serializer is the right-sized fix. Nothing already provides an export action. The only conflict is the owner row, which is a row question, not a framing one.

Since the code shows the owner row conflicts with the current column contract, here is how I propose to handle that row:

```text
Row: "The export includes the owner column." - src/export/csv.ts:40 lists only title and status.
A) in-scope - the export's column set becomes the table's columns plus owner, sourced from the report row's owner field
B) deviates: <why>
C) deferred: <where>
D) repair the ticket - /skill:shape-ticket acme/widgets#77 "The export includes the owner column." vs src/export/csv.ts:40 (tableColumns = ["title", "status"])
Recommendation: A - the row can ship in this gauntlet by extending only the export's column list. It flips to D if report rows turn out to carry no owner value.
```

## (2) Approaches message

First, two implicit dependencies are still open:

- **Owner value on report rows.** I looked for one in the files available, and `src/export/csv.ts:40` shows only `title` and `status`. I couldn't check this further, so it stays an assumption in Open Questions.
- **Existing paging.** Your answer says to reuse the existing paging. No paging code appears in the files I have, so I couldn't check it. The 10k-row, under-60s row depends on it, so it stays unverified and the plan must locate it first.

The button sits beside the report title, per your answer. The owner row is not settled in the recorded answers. The approaches below assume option A from the row question (in-scope, owner added to the export). If the answer differs, only the column-list part changes.

What separates the approaches is **where the owner column is defined and what produces the file.**

**Recommended: reuse the serializer and paging, with an export-only column list.** This matches your answer.

- The button beside the title calls the existing CSV serializer.
- The serializer pages through the report using the existing paging.
- The export's columns become `tableColumns` plus `owner`.
- The table itself stays unchanged.
- No new construct is added beyond the button and one column-list extension.
- The 10k-row, under-60s target is checked by a test that exports a 10k-row fixture and measures elapsed time.

Pattern: this follows the serializer's reuse of the table columns (`src/export/csv.ts:40`). It partly cuts across that pattern, because the export's column set now forks from the table's single definition. The spec will name that fork.

**Alternative: add owner to the shared table columns.** This drops the assumption that the table stays as it is. `owner` joins `tableColumns`, so the table and the export keep one column definition, and the serializer is reused unchanged. The cost is a visible table change the ticket never asked for.

Pattern: this keeps the single column-definition source at `src/export/csv.ts:40` intact.

**Alternative: a server-side streamed or background export job.** This drops the assumption that the existing paging can meet the 60s target in the request path. It adds a new export endpoint or job. That is a new construct, and it is only justified if paging proves too slow.

Pattern: it bypasses the existing serializer path at `src/export/csv.ts`, adding a second export route beside the one that already exists.

What would flip the recommendation:

- If you want owner visible in the table, or you see the forked column list as debt, switch to adding owner to the shared columns.
- If the existing paging can't be found, or misses 60s on 10k rows, switch to the streamed job.
